Requirement_Summary: PencilKit capture; validity requires >= 3 data points and >= 100 px stroke length; 'signature not valid' otherwise.

The CVR's own sample signature is not even this real -- it is a boolean stub (CLMViews.swift:1092-1094) with no capture UI at all.
Risk_Notes: Reuse the DragGesture/Canvas pattern (not PencilKit, contrary to spec wording, but functionally equivalent) and add the length/point validation that is currently entirely absent.

Requirement_Summary: Storage: avoid the benchmark's 32KB-field truncation -- store as ContentVersion (PNG) + compressed vector stroke JSON with SHA-256 hash; never truncate; enforce a sane max with a clear error.
SF_Evidence: Call_Visit_Report__c.Signature_Image__c is a Text(18) field storing a ContentDocument Id (not the image bytes themselves), so the org already avoids the 32KB truncation the spec warns about by design -- a real strength to reuse. However there is no vector-stroke JSON storage, no SHA-256 hash field anywhere (Ledger_Hash__c/Hash fields confirmed absent org-wide), and no Apex class was found that actually creates the ContentVersion for a CVR signature (only test code sets a hardcoded fake Id, SampleDropServiceTest.cls:61). By contrast, RCPA_Audit__c.Chemist_Signature__c is a 131,072-char LongTextArea storing a base64 PNG data URL -- exactly the truncation-prone anti-pattern the spec warns against, and a CONFLICT if reused as a model for samples.
iOS_Evidence: Signature strokes are never pushed to Salesforce at all today for Consent or RCPA (iOS inventory §6: 'Signature strokes deliberately never leave the device... only metadata... is sent'), and the CVR signature capture writes no image data whatsoever (it's a label-only stub).
Risk_Notes: The CVR's ContentDocument-Id design is the right pattern to build on; RCPA's LongTextArea base64 pattern must NOT be copied for samples (data-migration/compliance risk if it is).

Requirement_Summary: 'Request Receipt' checkbox + HCP email; after Accept, send an approved-template email receipt (queued offline, sent on sync); log delivery.

SF_Evidence: No dedicated 'opt-in required' indicator field/UI on the account/HCP layout beyond the generic Consent__c related list; SampleEligibilityService's opt-in warning is only surfaced as part of a line-level eligibility Result, not an Account-header badge.

Risk_Notes: AccountDetailsView.consentCard is a solid, directly reusable UI pattern to specialize for sample opt-in.

Requirement_Summary: In-person capture: customer ticks consent and signs; show validity period; save -> back to Account.
SF_Evidence: Consent__c stores Signed__c/Signed_At__c/Signer_Name__c/Sample_Opt_In_Valid_Until__c -- the data model supports this flow -- but no LWC/page implements an in-person consent-capture screen server-side (web channel).
iOS_Evidence: ConsentCaptureView.swift + SignatureSheet is a real, working in-person capture flow (channel toggles, real signature pad, submits back to Account on confirm) -- but it is generic multichannel consent, not specifically the sample-opt-in consent+validity-period UI the spec describes (no validity-period display, no Sample_Opt_In_Signature__c/Sample_Opt_In_Valid_Until__c write path).
Risk_Notes: ConsentCaptureView is the closest existing precedent and should be extended/forked for sample opt-in rather than built from scratch.

Requirement_Summary: Record in Sample_Consent__c: account, channel, captured by, captured date, valid from/to, signature, method flags (in-person/share-link/QR), consent text version.
SF_Evidence: Consent__c exists with HCP__c, Captured_At__c, Sample_Opt_In_Signature__c, Sample_Opt_In_Valid_Until__c, Signed__c/Signed_At__c/Signer_Name__c -- covers most of the shape as a single object rather than a dedicated Sample_Consent__c -- but is MISSING: a 'captured by' (rep) lookup field, a 'valid from' date (only 'valid until' exists), the three method flags (Captured_In_Person__c/Captured_Share_Link__c/Captured_QR_Code__c), and a consent-text-version field (field directory listing confirms none of these exist on Consent__c).
iOS_Evidence: ConsentRecord (Models/UserModels.swift:397-445) has capturedAt, signed, signerName, signatureMeaning, signedAt, signatureStrokes -- roughly parallel shape -- but likewise has no captured-by, valid-from, method flags, or text-version fields, and channels/products are keyed to email/mobile/whatsapp opt-in, not a sample-opt-in-specific structure.
Risk_Notes: Both platforms need the same four missing fields added in parallel; reuse Consent__c/ConsentRecord rather than building a wholly separate Sample_Consent__c object.

Requirement_Summary: Entry points: Account -> More Actions -> Sample Opt-In, or the opt-in warning on the Call.
SF_Evidence: No 'Sample Opt-In' specific action distinct from the generic 'Capture Consent' action anywhere; no Call-screen opt-in warning link (see SM-CALL-02).
iOS_Evidence: 'Capture Consent' action exists on both Account (AccountDetailsView.swift:237) and Call (CLMViews.swift:474) screens, giving both required entry points structurally -- but it opens the generic multichannel ConsentCaptureView, not a sample-opt-in-specific flow, and there is no opt-in warning banner on the Call to link from (see SM-CALL-02, MISSING).
Risk_Notes: Entry-point plumbing (menu items on both screens) already exists; only the destination screen needs to become sample-opt-in-aware.

Requirement_Summary: Signature Set Up screen: choose Share Link (email/SMS/WhatsApp) or QR Code -> Next -> prompts -> share.
SF_Evidence: No such screen/controller exists; no outbound SMS/WhatsApp integration exists in the org at all (SF inventory §9).
iOS_Evidence: No equivalent screen in the iOS app.
Risk_Notes: Depends on SM-OPT-07's remote-signing site existing first; SMS/WhatsApp channel is unimplemented anywhere (fields exist on Consent__c anticipating it, per SF inventory §9, but no working channel).

Requirement_Summary: HCP opens link/scans QR -> Salesforce Site/Experience Cloud page (no login, signed single-use token, expires in N minutes) -> reviews -> signs -> Accept.
SF_Evidence: No Experience Cloud/Sites/guest-user surface exists anywhere in this org's metadata -- confirmed absent (force-app/main/default/experiences|networks|sites|digitalExperiences all absent per SF inventory §8.4); this is a full greenfield build, and no token-signing/expiry mechanism exists either.
iOS_Evidence: This is inherently a server-hosted, non-app surface (the HCP does not use the iPad app); not applicable to the iOS client beyond triggering the send.
Risk_Notes: This is the single largest net-new build in this slice: a public guest site plus signed single-use tokens with expiry is genuinely new infrastructure, not an extension of anything existing.

Requirement_Summary: Rep sees confirmation (push + in-app via Platform Event/polling); reviews the signature; Accepts (creates consent, sets method checkbox) or Requests re-sign.
SF_Evidence: No Platform Event or polling mechanism for remote opt-in confirmation exists; Sample_Attempt__e is the only Platform Event in the org and is unrelated (blocked-sample-attempt logging).

Risk_Notes: Depends entirely on SM-OPT-07 existing; also exposes that the app has no real remote/APNs push channel today (LocalNotificationService is on-device-trigger only).

Requirement_Summary: Improvement over the benchmark: the remote request persists server-side so the rep can leave and accept later from a Pending Remote Signatures list.
SF_Evidence: No Pending Remote Signatures list/object exists.
iOS_Evidence: No equivalent list/screen exists.

Requirement_Summary: Prerequisites enforced: call-sampling enabled + opt-in-required config; FLS on consent fields.
SF_Evidence: SampleConfig.requireOptIn/optInHardBlock (from UCPMP_Tenant_Config__c) gate the check in SampleEligibilityService -- the config-driven prerequisite exists -- but FLS on Consent__c fields was not verified in this pass (SF inventory §1.15/permission-set notes flag Consent__c as having no Apex managed sharing, meaning every rep can see/edit every HCP's consent record today; FLS specifically is UNVERIFIED without a metadata-level profile/permset field-permission read).
iOS_Evidence: Client enforcement mirrors whatever server config says; no separate iOS-side prerequisite concept to assess beyond what SM-CALL-02/SM-OPT-01 already cover.
Risk_Notes: UNVERIFIED: FLS on Sample_Opt_In_Signature__c/Sample_Opt_In_Valid_Until__c needs an explicit profile/permission-set field-level-security check before relying on it for compliance; Consent__c's lack of Apex managed sharing (SF inventory §1.15/§10) is a real privacy gap worth flagging to compliance.

Requirement_Summary: Controlled-substance drops still require a signature despite a valid opt-in.
SF_Evidence: SampleEligibilityService.cls:65-67 hard-blocks when Product__c.Is_Controlled_Substance__c=true and the HCP has no Controlled_Substance_License__c, independent of opt-in status; and Needs_Signature__c (SampleDropService.cls:33) is forced true whenever Is_Controlled_Substance__c=true regardless of any opt-in state -- opt-in never bypasses this.
iOS_Evidence: No opt-in or controlled-substance concept exists client-side at all to conflict with this rule; nothing to assess (client simply lacks the whole feature).
Risk_Notes: Genuinely solid, already-correct server-side rule -- one of the better-covered requirements in this slice.

Requirement_Summary: Example UI test: rep captures annual opt-in for Dr. A remotely via share link; afterwards disburses samples without interruption for the validity period.
SF_Evidence: No test coverage for this scenario exists (SampleEligibilityServiceTest.cls exists for the eligibility check generally, but the remote-share-link opt-in flow it would need to test does not exist to be tested).
iOS_Evidence: No corresponding Swift/XCUITest coverage exists (the single existing UI test, SciagenCRMUITests.swift, is a shallow screenshot walkthrough with no functional assertions, per iOS inventory §9).
Risk_Notes: Cannot be written until SM-OPT-06/07/08 exist; track as an acceptance test once that infrastructure is built.

Requirement_Summary: Cold-chain = hand-carried samples needing refrigeration (Cold_Chain__c on product).
SF_Evidence: Product__c.Requires_Cold_Chain__c (boolean) exists and is read by SampleDropService.cls:22,51-56 to gate cold-chain-specific validation on every sample line.
iOS_Evidence: No cold-chain flag or concept anywhere in the ProductCatalogItem struct (Models/ProductCatalogModels.swift:25-45, confirmed by full-file read in iOS inventory) or any view.
Risk_Notes: Server flag is solid; iOS product model needs the field added as part of its (currently nonexistent) sample sync scope.

Requirement_Summary: Capture Tag Alert Number and Cold Chain Status at Receipt confirmation, Call sample, Transfer, Return, Adjustment.
SF_Evidence: Sample_Transaction__c (one object, Transaction_Type__c picklist covering Receipt/Transfer_Out/Transfer_In/Return/Adjustment/Disbursement) carries Cold_Chain_Status__c/Cold_Chain_Tag_Number__c/Cold_Chain_Temperature__c fields, so the single-object design already covers all transaction types structurally -- and Sample_Drop__c (the call-line object) also carries Cold_Chain_Status__c/Cold_Chain_Tag_Number__c with a hard-block in SampleDropService when missing on a cold-chain product. However the Sample_Transaction__c standard page layout exposes only Product/Quantity/Status/Transaction_Type/Name/Owner (verified by reading the layout XML directly) -- the cold-chain fields are not on the layout at any transaction-creation point, and no dedicated Transfer/Return/Adjustment/Receipt LWC exists to capture them either.
iOS_Evidence: No cold-chain capture at any point in the iOS app (no Transfer/Return/Adjustment/Receipt screens exist at all, and the samples card has no cold-chain fields).
Risk_Notes: This is a clear schema-exists-but-UI-missing gap on the SF side across every transaction type, and a total absence on iOS.

Requirement_Summary: iPad UX: arrow control opens Tag Alert Number selection (from Sample_Lot_Item__c TagAlert records or new entry), then Cold Chain Status selection.
SF_Evidence: Sample_Lot_Item__c (the TagAlert-record-type child object the spec calls for) does not exist anywhere in the org.
iOS_Evidence: No such UI pattern exists on iOS.
Risk_Notes: Needs the Sample_Lot_Item__c child object built first; current Cold_Chain_Tag_Number__c is a flat text field with no picklist-of-known-tags concept.

Requirement_Summary: Tag alert number validated by Tag_Alert_Regex.
SF_Evidence: No Tag_Alert_Regex CMDT setting or validation rule exists on Sample_Transaction__c/Sample_Drop__c/Sample_Lot__c cold-chain-tag fields (the 4 validation rules that do exist on Sample_Lot__c are all about quantity/expiry, not the tag number).
iOS_Evidence: No regex validation on the iOS side (no field exists to validate).
Risk_Notes: None.

Requirement_Summary: Required-ness of tag/status fields driven by layout config; validated if present on the layout.
SF_Evidence: SampleDropService.cls:51-53 does hard-require both Cold_Chain_Tag_Number__c and Cold_Chain_Status__c together (not either/or, and not layout-config-driven -- it's hardcoded in Apex) for any Requires_Cold_Chain__c=true product on a Sample_Drop__c line; there is no equivalent requiredness logic for Sample_Transaction__c (Receipt/Transfer/Return/Adjustment).
iOS_Evidence: Not applicable client-side since no cold-chain UI exists.
Risk_Notes: Existing Apex rule should be generalized into config-driven requiredness (SM-CFG-05-style) rather than hardcoded, and extended to the other transaction types.

Requirement_Summary: Status 'Excursion-Quarantine' blocks disbursement of that lot and prompts a Return.
SF_Evidence: SampleDropService.cls:52-53 blocks a line outright when Cold_Chain_Status__c='Breach' ('Cold chain breach detected. Cannot distribute. Return to warehouse for quality assessment.') -- functionally equivalent behavior exists, but the picklist value used is 'Breach' (Normal/Alert/Breach per Sample_Lot__c.Cold_Chain_Status__c's valueSet), not the spec's 'Excursion-Quarantine' naming, and there is no automatic prompt/action to create a Return record -- the message is advisory text only.
iOS_Evidence: Not applicable client-side (no cold-chain UI exists to be blocked).
Risk_Notes: Naming mismatch between org's Normal/Alert/Breach values and spec's OK/Excursion-Usable/Excursion-Quarantine values needs a compliance-sign-off decision (rename picklist vs. keep and remap in documentation).

Requirement_Summary: Document in the admin guide: integration changes needed for the new fields and the regression/validation testing regulatory will need.
SF_Evidence: Documentation deliverable, not a code artifact; no docs/samples/ADMIN_GUIDE.md exists yet in this repo (out of scope for this read-only gap audit to produce).
iOS_Evidence: Same -- documentation deliverable.
Risk_Notes: Purely a Phase-7 documentation task per the build spec's own delivery plan (§22); no code dependency.

Requirement_Summary: Custom text (e.g. voucher/co-pay card number) captured at Receipt, Disbursement, Transfer, Return, and on the Call line.
SF_Evidence: Custom_Text__c exists on both Sample_Drop__c (call line / disbursement) and Sample_Transaction__c (covers Receipt/Transfer/Return via Transaction_Type__c) -- schema-complete across all five capture points named in the spec -- but as with cold chain (SM-CC-02), the Sample_Transaction__c layout does not expose Custom_Text__c (layout XML confirmed to show only Product/Quantity/Status/Transaction_Type/Name/Owner) and the cvrSampleDrops LWC add form does not expose it either (only Product__c/Qty__c) -- no UI anywhere can currently set this field.
iOS_Evidence: No custom-text field exists anywhere in the iOS SampleDrop/transaction-adjacent models.
Risk_Notes: Same schema-exists/UI-missing pattern as cold chain and same fix (expose the field in the LWC forms and layouts, add to iOS SampleDrop).

Requirement_Summary: Enabled per product; required vs optional configurable; fixed label 'Custom Text' but configurable help text; reportable.
SF_Evidence: No Custom_Text_Enabled__c / Custom_Text_Required__c field exists on Product__c (field directory confirms absent), and no configurable help-text mechanism exists.
iOS_Evidence: Not applicable client-side (no custom-text UI exists to configure).
Risk_Notes: Needs the two Product__c flags added before the SM-CT-01 UI work can be made product-aware/conditional.

Requirement_Summary: High-value promo items (books/models/demo devices) need HCP signature; Alt Samples need valid license+signature; IN pack limits HV items per SM-PRD-06; block products flagged Personal_Benefit__c.
SF_Evidence: Needs_Signature__c computation (SampleDropService.cls:33, from Requires_Signature__c/Is_Controlled_Substance__c) is generic enough to cover an HV-item flag once one exists, and Alternative Sample behavior is already partially supported via Requires_Lot_Number__c=false (see SM-CALL-12) with license/signature checks still applied -- but there is no High-Value-Promotional-Item product type, no Unit_Value_INR__c cap, and critically no Personal_Benefit__c field/block anywhere in Product__c (grep confirmed absent), so UCPMP 8.1 gift-for-personal-benefit blocking does not exist at all.
iOS_Evidence: PromoDrop struct (CLMModels.swift:284-288) is item-name + qty only, with zero signature/value/personal-benefit distinction of any kind, and the promoCard UI (CLMViews.swift) has no signature requirement gate.
Risk_Notes: The Personal_Benefit__c hard-block (UCPMP 8.1) is a genuine compliance gap worth flagging prominently -- nothing today prevents a prohibited personal-benefit item from being logged as a promo drop.

Requirement_Summary: Product Order Allocation page date filter excludes allocations whose Start Date is more than Allocation_Date_Lookback_Years before the start of the current year.
SF_Evidence: No Allocation_Date_Lookback_Years config exists; the Sample_Allocation__c standard layout shows only Allocation_Quantity__c/Product__c/Status__c/Name/OwnerId (layout XML confirmed) -- it doesn't even expose Period_Start__c/Period_End__c, let alone filter by them; no dedicated allocation LWC exists in the 52-component lwc/ listing.
iOS_Evidence: Allocations are an admin/web feature per the build spec's screen map; not an iPad screen requirement in this build (SM-IOS-04 does list 'Allocations' as an iPad screen, so flagging PARTIAL-applicability, but no such screen exists in the current iOS app at all).
Risk_Notes: Sample_Allocation__c's own page layout is currently unusable for allocation management (missing Period_Start/End, Allocated_To_User/Territory, Used/Remaining Quantity) -- needs a proper LWC, not just a layout fix.

Requirement_Summary: Allocations sorted by Start Date descending; latest selected by default.
SF_Evidence: No allocation listing UI/LWC exists to sort at all.
iOS_Evidence: No iOS allocation screen exists.
Risk_Notes: Trivial once an allocation LWC/screen exists.

Requirement_Summary: Allocation Product filter shows only the products and Detail associated with the allocation.
SF_Evidence: No such filter UI exists.
iOS_Evidence: No iOS allocation screen exists.
Risk_Notes: None blocking beyond the general allocation-UI build.

Requirement_Summary: Allocation consumption decremented by disbursements/orders; over-allocation blocked.
SF_Evidence: SampleAllocationService.applyDisbursements() (52-line class, full read) correctly decrements/increments Sample_Allocation__c.Used_Quantity__c after every Disbursement transaction (called from SampleTransactionService.cls:308-309) and flips Status__c to 'Depleted' once Used_Quantity__c >= Allocation_Quantity__c -- real, working consumption tracking. But this runs strictly AFTER the disbursement transaction is created (post-hoc bookkeeping); no check anywhere in SampleEligibilityService/SampleDropService.beforeInsert consults Sample_Allocation__c before allowing a sample line, so 'over-allocation blocked' does NOT happen -- a rep can disburse past an exhausted allocation and it will simply be recorded as over-depleted after the fact.
iOS_Evidence: No iOS allocation concept exists to assess.
Risk_Notes: Consumption-tracking-without-blocking is a real functional gap (CONFLICT-adjacent): the spec explicitly requires blocking, and today there is none -- classified PARTIAL rather than CONFLICT because nothing contradicts the spec outright, it's simply an unimplemented half of the rule.

Requirement_Summary: Rep creates Inventory Orders (re-supply) with lines; approval -> warehouse/ERP integration -> shipment -> Receipt.
SF_Evidence: No Inventory_Order__c / Inventory_Order_Line__c object exists anywhere in the org; no warehouse/ERP outbound integration exists at all (SF inventory §9 confirms zero outbound callout infrastructure org-wide).
iOS_Evidence: No inventory-order concept anywhere in the iOS app (RCPA's Personal Order Booking, POBLine, is the closest analog -- a rep-initiated order with qty per SKU -- but it is a retail-chemist stock order, not a rep re-supply request, and per iOS inventory §5.1 has zero quota/governance logic).
Risk_Notes: RCPA's POB flow (RCPAViews.swift:762-820, POBLine model) is a structurally similar, directly reusable UI/data pattern (product picker + qty stepper + submit) worth adapting rather than building from zero.

Risk_Notes: Approval Process metadata being entirely unretrieved/UNVERIFIED org-wide (per SF inventory) is a cross-cutting risk: SM-INV-05, SM-ADJ-03 and similar approval-gated rules cannot be confirmed to work in the live org from source alone -- needs an org-level retrieve before design sign-off.

Requirement_Summary: Third-party auditors get a read-only 'Sample Auditor' permission set + audit inventory type; auditor counts enterable via web.
SF_Evidence: No Sample_Auditor (or similarly named) permission set exists among the org's 14 permission sets (full listing checked: Sciagen_Sample_Admin is the closest, but it is a read/write admin set, not the spec's dedicated read-only Sample_Auditor role named in SM-SEC-01 too).
